How we chose

Three rules, in this order.

1. $3,000 or less on i9Store today. The listed price on 26 Nov 2026, body only, before sales tax and shipping. If a price moves over the cap, the camera leaves the list at the next monthly re-read.

2. Made for filming. Each pick earns its place with features people who film use every day: RAW or log recording, high frame rates, stabilisation, two card slots or a vertical mount. Each card quotes the maker’s own spec page, with the date we read it. No scores from reviews we can’t show you.

3. Honest about the rest. Each pick says who it isn’t for. A body needs a lens, cards and batteries: the R6 V starter kit shows what a full kit costs. One camera many guides name, the Nikon ZR, isn’t sold by i9Store USA, and the page says so below.

Cameras under $3,000: questions.

Body prices, sensor sizes, RAW and the Nikon ZR.

Are these prices for the body only?

Yes, unless the name says a lens is included. They are i9Store’s listed USD prices, read on 26 Nov 2026, before sales tax and shipping. A lens, memory cards and a spare battery come on top: the R6 V starter kit shows a real total.

Full frame, Super 35 or APS-C: what changes?

A full-frame sensor (R6 V, R6 Mark III) is larger than a Super 35 or APS-C sensor (FX30, Pocket 6K G2, R50 V). With the same framing it gives a shallower depth of field, and the same lens frames tighter on the smaller sensor. Smaller sensors keep bodies and lenses cheaper.

Which of these record RAW video inside the camera?

The Canon EOS R6 V and R6 Mark III record 7K RAW (Light), and the Blackmagic Pocket 6K G2 records Blackmagic RAW. The Sony FX30 records XAVC HS and XAVC S, and the Canon EOS R50 V records XF-HEVC S or XF-AVC S.

Do I need a viewfinder?

Only if you frame at eye level, in bright sun or for stills. Of the five picks, only the EOS R6 Mark III has one built in; Blackmagic sells an optional OLED viewfinder for the Pocket 6K G2. The others are screen-only.

Why isn’t the Nikon ZR on this list?

i9Store USA doesn’t sell it: its listing on i9store.com/usa read “Product unavailable at i9Store USA” on 26 Nov 2026. Nikon USA lists it at “starting at $2,199.95”, under the cap. The Canon EOS R6 V vs Nikon ZR comparison puts the two side by side.
